course_description: This hands-on course introduces students manufacturing, assembly principles and prototyping in the design context. Prototyping is essential to create tangible versions of design ideas, test functionality with users, iterate and refine design concepts, and validate design ideas. In this course, students will learn about a range of materials and techniques (subtractive and additive manufacturing) to create physical prototypes used throughout the design process, enabling them to choose materials and prototyping methods to best respond to design requirements. Students will be introduced to emerging manufacturing technologies such as Computer Assisted Design (CAD) and 3D printing and apply their learnings to respond to a design brief. This course is an opportunity for students to familiarise themselves with a variety of CAD software with various functionalities relevant to the design industry.

restrictions: Restricted to students enrolled in the BDes, BDes dual programs, and the Design Thinking major

course_aims: This course aims to equip students with design fabrication capabilities required throughout the design process and necessary to materialise, test, and validate design ideas effectively.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise design manufacturing principles, materials, and technologies in the design context, and their impact on broader systems.
Communicate product design ideas using technical drawing conventions.
Experiment with and apply introductory subtractive and additive prototyping techniques based on design briefs
Use CAD models in digital fabrication processes to support prototyping and communicate design concepts
Justify use of prototyping methods to address specific design requirements across various contexts.
Communicate prototyping outcomes and design concepts effectively through written, visual, and verbal forms suited to peer audiences.

assessment_details.title: Prototyping Files
assessment_details.due_date: Part 1 27/08/2026 5:00 pm Part 2 9/09/2026 5:00 pm Part 3 7/10/2026 5:00 pm Digital Submission: Via Blackboard
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: Model all three (3) components of your trophy designed for the Design Award in Autodesk Fusion 360 that utilise the capabilities of each advanced prototyping technology. This is a 3-part submission that must include: Part 1 - 3D Printed Main Body (10%) You will use Autodesk Fusion to model the main form of your trophy that reflects your chosen design language. The form must be modelled within the constraints of and optimised for FDM 3D printing. Files must be ready for processing in .STL format – Renamed using the following naming convention: lastname_firstname_DSGN1400_AT23DP_part#of# Submit all native CAD file(s) and .STL file(s) in Blackboard. Part 2 – CNC-Machined Base (10%) Using Autodesk Fusion, model the base of your trophy so that it expresses your chosen design language and can be CNC-machined from a solid block Two distinct outputs, each demonstrating a different skill: Manufacturability (CAM). Production geometry (STEP). Export the final base model as a STEP file (.stp), the neutral 3D format the workshop uses to drive machining. You will submit the following files to Blackboard: Native Fusion file (.f3d) containing your CAM setup STEP file (.stp) of the final base A short screen-capture of the simulated toolpath (roughing + finishing) File naming: lastname_firstname_DSGN1400_AT23DP_part#of# Part 3 – Laser Cut Packaging (10%) You will use Autodesk Fusion’s Sheet Metal tools to design packaging that reflects your chosen design language. You will need to create a dieline of your design to be laser cut. Files must be ready for processing in .DXF format – Renamed using the following naming convention: lastname_firstname_DSGN1400_AT23DP_part#of#. Submit all native CAD file(s) and .DXF file(s) in Blackboard. assessment_details.title: Design Trophy: Final Design and Artefact
assessment_details.due_date: Digital Submission 28/10/2026 5:00 pm Presentation and Exhibition in class 29/10/2026
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: Tangible artefact and presentation due in class. In this project, you are invited to design and prototype a trophy for the Design Award. You will submit your final physical trophy design with the following outputs: 1. Behance Project Page (Design Documentation) Create a Behance profile and upload one project that presents your trophy design. Include your final renders, your process work, and both animations. Your project page must include: A clear project title and a short introduction (2–3 sentences) explaining what the trophy is for and your design idea. Final renders in high resolution: at least one hero image and 2–3 additional views, all with clean and consistent backgrounds. Process work showing how your design developed (sketches, iterations, key decisions). A short animation showing your trophy rotating 360 degrees (export from Fusion or similar software). 2. Process Video (Design Process and Development) Create a short video explaining how your design developed from initial idea to the design outcome. Video should include: Early sketches and initial ideas Key design decisions and why you made them Iterations and how your design changed over time Your final design outcome 2. Physical Trophy (In-Class Presentation) Bring your completed trophy to class for display and presentation for a 5-minutes presentation.
